evidence.label: def:p15-measurement-target: measurand (object, conditions, interpretation), realization, result = estimate + units + uncertainty; definitional uncertainty distinct from repeat variation
Sheet thickness at a reference temperature with calibration, temperature and compression corrections; steel-bar specification depends on accuracy [D.1-D.5, 3.1.3]

def:p15-measurement-error: error y-v, correction -b, standard uncertainty is not the realized error, the correction or a bound; recognized effects corrected and their uncertain corrections kept in the model; Figs D.1-D.2 reading
def:p15-measurement-model: chosen units/coordinates, input vector X, output Y=f(X), estimates x and assessed covariance U
Input roles (calibration values, corrections, influence quantities, reference data); power model with named inputs V, R0, alpha, t, t0 and sensitivities
Uncertain voltmeter correction (uniform half-width 15 uV) combined with the 12 uV mean at 0.928571 V

End gauge: explicit measurand (length at 20 deg C, nominal 50 mm), measurement equation, units, per-input role table incl. comparator random-/systematic-effect corrections; thermal corrections estimated zero with nonzero uncertainty
Result with units: l = 50.000838 mm, u_c ~ 34 nm, relative 6.8e-7
Observed random variation is not the whole uncertainty; systematic corrections also needed
def:p15-measurement-procedure steps 1-3: measurand, units, reference conditions; equation with corrections and influence quantities; inputs with information sources
Held JCGM 100:2008 3.1.3 (PDF p.16): steel-bar specification example; matches body 43-45

Held JCGM 100:2008 D.3.2-D.3.4 (PDF p.61-62): sheet thickness, realized quantity, corrections; matches body 36-42
thm:p15-measurement-affine-covariance: Cov(a+JX) = J Sigma J^T; scalar form with 2 sum c_i c_j Sigma_ij; uncorrelated suffices
Written proof: Y-EY = J(X-m), outer-product expectation gives J Sigma J^T, scalar expansion, PSD and correlation bounds, +1 and zero-correlation cases
First-order u_lin^2 = c^T U c with covariance/correlation terms; J U J^T with off-diagonals; neither full-correlation nor RSS is the general rule
Shared calibration influence: Var(A-B), Var(A+B), dropping covariance wrong; ten resistors give 1 ohm, not sqrt(10) 0.1 ohm
thm:p15-measurement-common-correction: exact Var(A+BQ) including v_B v_Q omitted at first order
thm:p15-measurement-taylor-bound: approximation conditions (C^2, Hessian norm <= M on convex set, finite 4th moment) and bounds on mean, remainder and |Var f(X) - Var L|
Written proof: integral Taylor remainder, |R| <= M||delta||^2/2, Cauchy-Schwarz on Cov(L,R)
First-order boundary: separate mean check, Gaussian next-order terms require remainder control, zero-gradient countercase
Impedance Jacobian, J U J^T, first-order results with and without input covariances
Held JCGM 100:2008 5.1.2 (PDF p.31): law of propagation rests on first-order Taylor; note on higher-order terms for normal inputs; matches body 311-319, 446-450
Held JCGM 100:2008 5.2.2 (PDF p.33-34): correlated combined variance (13)/(16), r=+1 note, ten resistors 1 ohm vs 0.32 ohm; matches body 311-340

def:p15-measurement-type-ab: Type A = statistical analysis of observation series; Type B = certificate, specification, previous data, justified bounded-influence model; labels classify methods, not random/systematic effects or reliability
Common probabilistic treatment of both information sources is an interpretive model choice [4.1.1, 4.1.6, E.3]
Type A information: mean/covariance theorem, s/sqrt(n), pooled s_p and its degrees of freedom, twenty-temperature data

Type B information: declared bounded distributions, support interval does not entail uniform, max-entropy asymmetric case, conversions from certificate multiples, stated intervals and bounds; no double counting
One model W = A + BQ: a priori offset/scale with Type A mean; E.3.4-E.3.7 distinction; identical variance algebra conditional on joint probabilistic interpretation; E.3.5 bet qualified
End-gauge budget: repeated-reading, certificate, bound and sine-model evaluations attached to one measurement model
Written proofs of the sample-covariance and bounded-distribution results
Written proof of the common-correction variance
Held JCGM 100:2008 3.3.3-3.3.5 (PDF p.18-19): A/B by method, not substitutes for random/systematic; a correction may be Type A or B; both rest on probability distributions
Held JCGM 100:2008 E.3.4-E.3.7 (PDF p.68-69): offset/scale model (E.6), traditional random/systematic labels, degree-of-belief bets, classify methods not components
Held JCGM 100:2008 4.1.6 (PDF p.22): Type A frequency-based vs Type B a priori distributions, both models of knowledge
def:p15-measurement-expanded: U = k u_c; a probability needs a distributional interpretation, a confidence claim needs sampling coverage
thm:p15-measurement-coverage-models: same k gives 2Phi(k)-1 (normal), min{k/sqrt3,1} (uniform), 2z-z^2 (triangular), only 1-k^-2 (Chebyshev)
Written proof of the coverage formulas and Chebyshev bound
k=2 normal ~0.9545 not exact 95%; multiplier adds no information; Student guarantee not general; effective df is moment matching only; Type B reliability convention
Written proof of the effective-df moment matching
Nonlinear countercase: X uniform on [-a,a], linearized x^2 gives zero estimate and zero variance; true mean a^2/3, variance 4a^4/45
Linear-budget nu_eff 16.7 -> 16, t ~ 2.92 does not give a 99% interval for the completed nonlinear calculation
Procedure step 6: state multiplier, probability interpretation and justification
Held JCGM 100:2008 6.2-6.3 (PDF p.35-36): U = k u_c, level of confidence uncertain, k=2 ~95% only for approximately normal output with sizeable nu_eff; matches body 468-498
Held JCGM 100:2008 G.4.1-G.4.2 (PDF p.85-86): Welch-Satterthwaite as approximation, nu_i from reliability (25% -> 8, 50% -> 2); matches body 512-520
Held JCGM 100:2008 H.1.6-H.1.7 (PDF p.96-97): nu_eff 16.7 -> 16, t99(16)=2.92, second-order terms raise u_c 32 -> 34 nm; matches body 588-623

defect_observations.observation: Power example: P is never named (source 4.1.1: power dissipated at temperature t, the measurand). No units are given. t and t0 appear only as 'temperatures', although the source makes t0 the defined temperature of R0. The text never says which factor is the uncertain correction its title announces. The C01 credit rests on the end-gauge section instead.

End gauge: l, d, alpha, theta and theta_S are never defined in words, unlike source H.1.1 (theta, theta_S are deviations from 20 deg C; l_S is the certificate value). The budget's Evaluation column gives divisors but not the information behind them: certificate k=3, comparator certificate at 95% from 6 replicates, 'three sigma' statement, rectangular bounds, 'supplied' bed temperature. The divisor 10 nm/2.57 is Student t95(5) (H.1.3.2), never explained, and it sits beside the 2.58 normal 99% divisor at line 270.

The Taylor-bound theorem states its variance bound through Var(L) at the mean m with covariance Sigma. It never writes Var(L) = Df(m) Sigma Df(m)^T and never relates (m, Sigma) to the pair (x, U) used in the first-order formula at lines 311-316. The reader must apply thm:p15-measurement-affine-covariance to L; the annex does this explicitly only for the impedance case (lines 335-336).

Proof of thm:p15-measurement-gaussian-expansion: Cov(A,C) is asserted with 'Similarly' (the pairings are named, the sum is not written), and Var(B) is described rather than computed. This is not on an owed derivation path for these components, but the step is compressed.

The thermal-product model assumes A, Theta, B and D are mutually independent. It does not repeat the H.1.2 caution that in the original coordinates (theta, theta_S, alpha, alpha_S) the correlations must be included, and it does not say why the reparametrization isolates the shared bed temperature.
